items.title: Mike Vax interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2022
items.q: when Stan was sick that first time in 1971 and he was gone for five months, Dick Shearer and I led the band and Dick led the music and conducted and I did all of the announcing

ctx.x: And I have to tell you, there’s a great story — at one point we were doing a panel discussion, it was Stan and Dick Shearer and I. And they were talking about, you know, liking to have — some of the teachers were talking about, you know, having doctorates and all that. And Stan really started talking about how important it was that teachers, that musicians who knew how to teach that had been on the road, that really understood what the music business is like and what it’s like to be a road musician. He said you…

Aw, you know I think you have some nerve in a positive way. Because I was reading the thing, this beautiful thing you wrote recently on FaceBook and you said that in 1960 you went to the Second National Stage Band Camp and afterwards you went up to Stan Kenton and said, “I’m going to play lead trumpet in your band.”
